overview.description: Authors is a classic memory-based card game where players compete to collect complete sets (books) of four cards of the same rank. Unlike 'Go Fish,' where players ask for a whole rank, Authors requires the precision of asking for a specific card by both rank and suit. It rewards keen observation and a sharp memory of which cards have been requested and by whom.

history.origins: Originally published in 1861 by G.M. Whipple and A.A. Smith in Salem, Massachusetts. The original set featured cards with names of famous authors and their book titles (e.g., Charles Dickens and 'Oliver Twist').
timeline: 1861: The game 'Authors' is first published in the USA.
Late 1800s: Becomes a standard 'improving' educational game for children.
1900s: Adapted to the standard 52-card deck, where 'Books' became card ranks instead of literary works.
Present: Still popular in Europe as 'Quartets' or 'Happy Families'.
history.evolution: The transition from specifically printed 'Author' sets to the standard deck allowed it to become a universal parlor game.
history.cultural: Used historically to teach literature and history; now primarily a foundational game for building children's logic and memory skills.

setup.equipment: Standard pack, score sheet for counting books.
setup.dealing: The entire deck is dealt out as evenly as possible. Some players may have one more card than others.

rules.objective: Capture the most 'Books' (sets of all four cards of a single rank).
rules.gameplay: 1. **Inquiry**: On your turn, you ask a specific player for a specific card (rank and suit), for example: 'Sarah, do you have the Nine of Diamonds?'. 2. **Prerequisite**: You can only ask for a card if you already hold at least one card of that same rank. 3. **The Exchange**: If the player has the card, they MUST hand it over. You then get another turn to ask anyone for another card. 4. **The End of Turn**: If the player does not have the card, your turn ends immediately and passes to the left. 5. **Completing a Book**: As soon as you hold all four suits of a rank, you must lay them face down on the table as a 'Book'.
keyRules: No Lying: If asked for a card you hold, you must give it up immediately.
Rank Constraint: You cannot ask for a card of a rank you do not have.
The End State: The game continues until all 52 cards have been organized into 13 books.

strategy.basic: Remember what other people ask for. If Tom asks Sarah for the Jack of Spades and Sarah doesn't have it, you now know Tom has a Jack and Sarah does not have the Jack of Spades.
strategy.intermediate: The Bluff: If you hold three Kings and need the fourth, ask someone who you know DOESN'T have it to end your turn, making others think you are weak on Kings. (Risky, as someone might target you next).
strategy.advanced: Elimination Mapping: Mentally track every revealed suit of a rank. If you see the Jack of Spades and Jack of Hearts go to one player, and you hold the Jack of Clubs, you only need to find the Jack of Diamonds to swoop the whole set.
tips: Pay attention even when it's not your turn. The information revealed during other people's turns is essential for winning.
Collect 'quietly'. Don't ask for the same rank three times in a row unless you are sure you can complete the book on that turn.

list.name: Go Fish Style
list.description: Played with a stock (boneyard). If the player doesn't have the card, you 'fish' from the deck.
list.emptyOverridesReason: This Go Fish style variant would need its own engine model; here it is documented only as a rules description.

list.name: Literature
list.description: A much more complex version played in teams where you ask for ranks from teammates and opponents.
list.emptyOverridesReason: Literature is a related partnership game with different structure, so it is listed here without engine overrides.

difficulty.easy: Asks for cards randomly from ranks it holds. Has no memory of what happened on previous turns.
difficulty.medium: Remembers who has cards that it needs. Will always ask a known holder first.
difficulty.hard: Maintains a full probability map of all 52 cards. Knows exactly who does NOT have a card based on their previous failed asks.

considerations: AI must implement a 'Knowledge-base' of negative information (e.g., 'Player A does not have Rank X Suit Y').
Memory depth should be configurable to simulate human-like forgetting.

ante.reason: Authors is a collection game with no betting or ante.

deal.reason: Dealing is done via custom deal_all_even action; no generic deal action.

reveal_market.reason: No market pile; entire deck is dealt to players at start.

buy_market.reason: There is no market or purchase mechanic in Authors.

buy_stock.reason: Whole deck is dealt out; no stock to buy from after deal.

fold.reason: Players ask for cards until turn ends; no fold action.

check.reason: No betting rounds; check does not apply to this game.

call.reason: No betting; call is not used in Authors.

bet.reason: Winning is by collecting the most books; no wagering.

raise.reason: No betting; raise does not apply to this game.

declare.reason: No declaration phase; players ask for specific cards only.

reveal_hand.reason: Cards are revealed only when asked for; no full reveal-hand phase.

award_pot.reason: No pot; winner is the player with the most books at game end.

play_card.reason: Play is by asking for cards via custom ask_specific_card action.

draw.reason: Entire deck is dealt at start; no drawing after deal in Authors.

discard.reason: Cards are transferred to asker or laid as books; no discard pile.

pass.reason: Turn ends when ask fails; no explicit pass action.

bid.reason: No bidding; play proceeds by asking for specific cards.

meld.reason: Books are sets of four same-rank cards laid down; no meld declaration.

go_out.reason: Game ends when all cards are in books; winner has most books.

engine.deckDescription: One standard 52-card deck consisting of four suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs), each with thirteen ranks from ace down to two. No jokers; used for this matching and collecting game where players complete sets of four (authors).
engine.suitDescription: Four French suits (spades, hearts, diamonds, clubs). In Authors, players ask for cards by rank; suit is used only to identify the specific card. All four suits are equal for forming books of four.
engine.rankDescription: Thirteen ranks per suit: ace, king, queen, jack, ten, nine, eight, seven, six, five, four, three, two. Players collect sets of four cards of the same rank (e.g. all four aces) to form books.

hero.title: AUTHORS
hero.subtitle: A Game of Perfect Memory
hero.tagline: Sharpen your mind. Spot the patterns. Complete the books.

synthesis.shortDescription: The classic Victorian card game of observation and memory. Step up from Go Fish by asking for specific suits, tracking opponent requests, and building your collection of complete sets in this timeless family favorite.

prompts.human: Welcome to Authors! You've been dealt your hand. You have the 7 of Clubs. That means you can ask anyone for any other 7. If you're right, you keep going! Pay attention to what Sarah asks Tomâ€”it's the only way to win.
prompts.ai: Game: Authors. Type: Memory / Collection. Rules: Whole deck dealt. Ask specific card (rank+suit). Must have same rank. If successful, repeat. Goal: Collect books of 4.

scoring.winCondition: The player with the most books at the end wins.

penalties.Illegal Ask: If you ask for a card and it is discovered you do not hold a card of that rank, you forfeit your next turn (house rule).

nullReasons.targetScore: No fixed target score; play ends when all 52 cards form 13 books and the player with the most books wins.
nullReasons.cardValues: Authors scores purely by completed books, so individual cards do not have separate point values.
